## Observed defect and immutable source
At current default commit `bc25f88ba645845dab32a6456da4129bd9d9d141`, the inline [release merge wait](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/bc25f88ba645845dab32a6456da4129bd9d9d141/.github/workflows/release.yml#L476-L595) initializes `awaiting_approval=0` before the loop, sets it to 1 whenever pending CI was observed (line583), and never clears it when a later poll has no approval-pending runs. Successful automatic approval still selects that assignment. The timeout conditional at588 therefore reports historical approval as current.

## Hosted evidence and bounded reproduction
The [release job126622927584](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/actions/runs/41839394513/job/126622927584) records at14:52:07 UTC on November4: `Approved workflow run 41851792106; its checks can now report.` At15:21:58 its final diagnostic nevertheless says the release PR did not merge because its CI run awaits approval and asks the maintainer to approve it once.

The exact [CI run41851792106](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/actions/runs/41851792106), on release-candidate head `f38eb8b8471ece88a6308764ca37bc663ffcb8e3`, is completed/success in a fresh15:38 UTC read. This is evidence against presenting the old approval warning as a current remedy. It does not establish every required check or review was satisfied at timeout.

An isolated Bash probe extracted the immutable workflow's exact timeout conditional and exit (lines588–595). It supplied two synthetic polling states: a run encountered and successfully approved, followed by an empty approval-pending set. Because the source retains the historical flag, the extracted branch still prints the approval-required error and exits1. The probe executed no GitHub API, approval, merge, publication or tag command and does not replay the entire release workflow.

## Source goal, expected/actual and impact
The canonical [pm-jev-uqu6 record](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/bc25f88ba645845dab32a6456da4129bd9d9d141/.agents/pm/issues/pm-jev-uqu6.toon), delivered through PR7, implements best-effort CI approval with scoped run matching and useful diagnostics when approval cannot be performed. It does not cover clearing stale approval state after success.

Expected: name approval as the remaining remedy only when current evidence establishes an unresolved approval. Otherwise report settling/missing/failed checks or reviews without attributing them to old approval state.

Actual: one historical pending-run observation permanently selects the approval-needed timeout branch. This sends maintainers toward an already approved run and hides the useful alternative diagnostic. The release job explicitly reports nothing published or tagged; preserve that fail-closed behavior. This is a diagnostic defect, not proof that correcting it permits a merge or publishes a package.

## Deduplication and limits
Reviewed all88 all-status GitHub issue/PR bodies,48 canonical PM records, and fresh conversations on release PR82 and PR88. No existing pm-jev issue owns this sticky-state diagnostic. Existing issue68 concerns release identity replacement and issue62 concerns the local tarball publish argument. The prior closed approval feature is distinct from this later failure. Analogous inline-copy defects are already tracked in pm-web298, pm-linear200, pm-ado84 and a pm-csv226 comment; this report is the affected pm-jev copy. No security-setting change, approval bypass, merge, rerun or publication is requested.

## Acceptance / regression criteria
- Successful approval followed by no currently pending runs must not print an approval-needed instruction.
- A currently action-required run whose approval failed remains identified with its verified run URL.
- Queued/running, missing, failed or cancelled checks are described from current evidence rather than historical approval state.
- Approval-state lookup failure stays explicitly unknown, not a confirmed empty or approved set.
- Test transitions across polling iterations, including successful and failed approvals, not only a constant flag.
- Preserve existing repository/main/opt-in guards and refusal to publish/tag before protected merge and artifact checks succeed.
Release timeout asks for workflow approval after automatic approval succeeded
